devils_advocate: Objection 1: Maybe escapeHtml() on tldr fields is a deliberate XSS-defense choice; any HTML in the source is intentionally-escaped output. Response: (a) c7 and c8 both explicitly frame the escape as a bug not a feature — the design intent stated in both reviews is 'HTML markup renders as escaped text (bug)'. (b) The parallel detail_evidence and detail_verdict_text fields are inserted un-escaped and DO render HTML (that is where the <sub> tags in `tan(lat<sub>BOU</sub>)` live successfully elsewhere on the page). Treating tldr differently to those two adjacent fields is inconsistent with the site pattern. (c) An allow-list sanitizer preserves XSS defense while permitting the small set of tags the review copy actually uses.

Objection 2: Maybe WIN-044.tldr_evidence should be treated as an isolated one-off — do the content patch and skip the systemic fix. Response: The systemic fix is the entire point of c8's major-severity finding. The content patch alone is exactly the mode of failure c8 predicted ('per-WIN workaround; next edit silently regresses'). Deferring option (b) again just resets the regression clock.

Objection 3: The fresh-eyes finding may be over-scoped for Mode 6 — the analyst is not supposed to remediate build pipeline bugs. Response: Correct — this is a surfacing pass, not a fix. The EXP proposes patches for the decider (option a is a 2-line find/replace; option b is a source-code change the decider routes for review). Mode 6 discipline (READ-ONLY) is honored: no direct mutation of wins.json, generate-html.js, or the tracker.
kernel_of_truth: The escapeHtml() calls at generate-html.js:880 and :892 are structurally the right defense against unknown/adversarial input. TLDR fields are user-visible copy and should get the same XSS protection every other content field gets. The problem is scope: we want XSS defense AND allow a small set of formatting tags. That is exactly what a sanitizer (not a plain escape) provides. c8's option (b) is not a rejection of the defensive intent; it is a refinement of the defense.
